_what: One row per inbound channel. This is the connection register: what the mechanism is, what we control, what the provider controls, what is still missing, and who has to do something about it. Nothing here activates anything. A channel becomes live by configuring credentials and a webhook at the provider, verifying, and switching mode from test to live - not by changing code.

_readiness.not_prepared: No adapter exists on our side.
_readiness.ready_for_configuration: Our side is finished. It needs credentials and a provider setting, nothing more.
_readiness.waiting_for_external_access: Our side is finished but somebody outside this repository must grant access, approve an app, or answer a question first.
_readiness.manual_only: The provider offers no inbound mechanism we can rely on. A person enters it by hand, and that is the design, not a gap.
_readiness.capability_unconfirmed: We do not know whether the provider can do this. EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED before anything is promised.

_modes: Every channel has a mode: off, test or live. Only 'test' accepts a simulated payload. 'live' additionally requires real credentials to be present, and nothing in this repository can set it.
_idempotency: Every adapter declares an externalId, and receive() in src/intake.js looks for an inbound row with the same channel and external_id before inserting, so the same provider event delivered twice is stored once. Providers retry; that is normal and must never make two people. CORRECTED 27.09.2026: this used to say a unique index enforces it. NO SUCH INDEX EXISTS - it is a look-then-insert check in application code. That is sound on SQLite, where one process runs one request at a time, and NOT sound on PostgreSQL behind Vercel, where two retries of one event can run at once, both look, both find nothing and both insert. The fix - a partial unique index on (channel, external_id) plus an insert that tolerates the conflict - is part of the PostgreSQL move. See docs/BACKLOG.md, 27.09.2026.

Configure OAuth and the API access

gmail.reconciliation: The poll IS the re-read, but it looks back a fixed 15 minutes and takes at most 25 messages, so a missed run or a busy window loses mail. A history-id cursor would close that. Not built.
gmail.review_27_09: BUILT ONLY TO THE FETCH. lib/gmail.js reads messages and api/cron/gmail-poll.js returns them in its reply; NOTHING passes them to receive(), so no email reaches the Inbox yet. Also an open decision the review raised: domain-wide delegation lets the service account read ANY mailbox in the Workspace with that scope - the code chooses one, the grant does not limit it. OAuth on a dedicated mailbox limits it to that mailbox. Ritvars and Marina decide.

phone._answered: ANSWERED 24.09.2026, and it was in the brief all along. The event carries a `queue` field, and the queue IS the button: 1001*Q-ADMISSION is button 1, 1001*Q-COORDINATORS is button 2, 1001*Q-OTHER is button 3. config/prototype.json -> phoneMenu has mapped it since 23.09.2026. It was listed as an open question by mistake and Ritvars had to point that out.

Connect the production PBX polling schedule
Use the existing confirmed button and queue mapping

phone.ownerAction: Put the token he holds into PBX_API_TOKEN, then configure the poll
phone.reliability: Poll every 5 minutes for the last 15, so two missed runs lose nothing; upsert on uniqueid absorbs the overlap.
phone.reconciliation: The overlap window is the reconciliation.
phone.review_27_09: TWO GAPS, 27.09.2026. (1) NO TRIGGER: the Vercel team is on Hobby, which rejects any cron more frequent than daily, so the 5-minute cron was removed from vercel.json; something else must call /api/cron/pbx-calls every 5 minutes before this channel goes live. (2) Calls are written by lib/pbx.js into its own table, pbx_incoming_calls, through the Supabase REST API. Nothing in src/ reads that table, so no call reaches the Inbox yet. Still worth asking TeleGroup whether a reliable call-event push exists (open question 9); if not, polling stays - it works.

_integrations: Added 29.09.2026. An INTEGRATION is not a channel. A channel receives a message from a person and needs an adapter; an integration is a system we pull from on a schedule. SIS was briefly put in `channels` and the contract test caught it at once: every channel in the register must have an adapter, and SIS has none because nothing is delivered to us. It appears on the Channels screen beside the channels, because that is where somebody looks to see whether anything is coming in, but it is modelled apart.

sis.reconciliation: sync_state holds the cursor and what the last run did.

_meta: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp are reached through ONE Meta Business Suite connection. That is an integration detail. Each remains a SEPARATE channel in the CRM for reporting, filtering, source and history: there is deliberately no combined "Meta" number, because it would hide where people actually came from. WhatsApp being inside the same shared inbox is NOT VERIFIED and must not be claimed.
_blockerKind: question = somebody outside has to answer and the answer may be no. work = the steps are known and nobody has done them yet. A "question" blocker must have an owner in prototype.json -> openQuestions, or nobody chases it. A test enforces that.
_connectOrder: The order Ritvars set on 24.09.2026. Both the Desktop guide and docs/CHANNEL_READINESS.md render in this order, so his list and the generated documents cannot drift apart.
_ownerPerson: Who physically has to act for each channel, told by Ritvars on 25.09.2026. null means nobody is named yet. This is NOT who owns the CRM record - a confirmed study lead always belongs to Admissions, which is Ieva, whatever channel it arrived on.
_reliability: Added 27.09.2026 after an outside architecture review. Getting an event once is not enough; each channel has to answer: did we get it, did we get it twice, did we process it, what if processing failed, what if the provider retries, what if the CRM was down, can we reconstruct what happened. 'reliability' says what protects the channel TODAY, read from the code. 'reconciliation' says how something missed would be found again, and says 'none built' where that is the truth. Three gaps are shared by every channel and are not repeated per row: (1) the dedupe is not database-enforced (see _idempotency); (2) the log of refused and failed deliveries is an in-memory list of 500 in src/server.js, lost on every restart and, on Vercel, different on every instance - so a refused or failed delivery leaves NO durable trace; (3) a delivery that fails inside the CRM answers 500, which makes a retrying provider try again, but nothing records that it failed.
_lifecycle: Added 02.10.2026. readiness says whether OUR SIDE is technically ready. lifecycle says whether the PRODUCT HAS THIS CHANNEL AT ALL, which is a decision and not an engineering fact. active = a channel we intend to connect. parked = decided, prepared, deliberately not connected yet; it is not work and nobody holds it. dropped = decided out of the product; the adapter may stay in the repository, the channel does not exist. Anything without this field is active. A screen MUST read lifecycle, never readiness, to decide whether a channel is current work.
